clue.text: Joint camp launch in chaos, so many changes to be made here

definitions.text: so many changes to be made here

indicators.note: letters in chaos are thrown into disorder, so the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shared camp's opening descends into a muddle with countless alterations needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' looks like general upheaval, but here it means changing trains. CLAPHAM JUNCTION is a huge, busy railway interchange in south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapham Junction is famous as Britain's busiest rail interchange, where vast numbers of passengers switch trains.

clue.text: Liable to forget one's problem

parts.note: read straight, someone apt to overlook a difficulty; cryptically, a person whose very problem is forgetting

explanation.surface: Someone tends to let their troubles slip their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a carefree person dodging worries; the cryptic reading is a person whose condition is memory loss itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesiac suffers memory loss, so forgetting is literally that person's medical problem.

clue.text: Soldiers, perhaps: GI avoids huge types

indicators.note: the GI stays away from the word, so those letters are taken out of it

parts.note: giants are huge people
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American soldier steers clear of very large characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldiers' are not troops here but the worker caste of an insect colony; 'perhaps' marks them as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldier ants are a caste in many ant colonies, so soldiers are an example of the insects.

clue.text: Reduce intensity? No we don't, unfortunately

indicators.note: things going unfortunately go wrong, so these letters end up in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks if we should lower the volume, and the reply is a regretful refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: To tone down something is to moderate it, making it softer or less extreme.

clue.text: After short pause, signal recovery

indicators.note: the signal word comes after the shortened pause in the answer
a short word is cut off before its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a rest is a pause
a cue is a signal to act

explanation.surface: After a brief halt, someone gives a sign that recovery is under way.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescue is the recovery of someone or something from danger, as in a mountain rescue.

clue.text: Musical direction we hear written out badly

indicators.note: what we hear is the spoken sound, so the word is taken by how it is pronounced

parts.note: the word said aloud, which loses its silent W and one T in the spelling

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musical instruction, read aloud, is transcribed poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' sounds out RITEN; 'badly' turns OUT into UTO. RITENUTO is an Italian musical term.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritenuto is an Italian tempo marking telling performers to hold back the pace suddenly.

clue.text: Said noble is without hope of heir

indicators.note: something said is spoken aloud, so the word is taken by its pronunciation

parts.note: a baron is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A spoken claim that an aristocrat has no prospect of a successor.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren describes someone unable to have children, so there is no hope of producing an heir.

clue.text: People in SUVs? Ones like Virginia — heavens!

parts.note: a fanciful coinage: those riding in jeeps would be jeepers
Virginia creeper is a climbing plant, so it is one of the creepers

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about who rides in sport utility vehicles, then a woman's name and an exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virginia' looks like a woman or a US state, but it is the climbing plant Virginia creeper.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeepers creepers is a dated exclamation of surprise, much like crying out goodness or heavens.

clue.text: Fish and fruit wonderful in Spain

parts.note: lemons are fruit
Spaniards shout olé to cheer something wonderful

explanation.surface: A meal of fish with fruit, praised as marvellous in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon sole is a flatfish commonly sold in Europe, related to plaice and flounder.

clue.text: To be mad not having succeeded is foolish

indicators.note: the word does without the following letter, so it is removed

parts.note: insane means mad
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: Being crazy without having achieved anything is plain silly.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly or senseless, lacking any sign of intelligence.

clue.text: Printing house that is making a gift

parts.note: a press is a printing house or publisher
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A printing firm produces a present.
explanation.walkthrough: PRESSIE is informal British slang for a present.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressie is a chummy British shortening of present, meaning something given.

clue.text: Become fine again? Explain

definitions.meaning: weather is said to ... when it turns sunny after rain
to ... a mystery is to explain it

explanation.surface: Someone asks if it will brighten up, and then asks for an explanation.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both skies brightening after bad weather and resolving confusion over something.

clue.text: A team of detectives is sharp

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the UK police detective branch

explanation.surface: A squad of detectives is quick-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid remark or taste is sharp, biting and tart.

clue.text: Favouring English athlete: one came first

parts.note: to be for something is to favour it
a runner is a track athlete

explanation.surface: Backing an English athlete who won the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came first' suggests winning a race, but it means preceded in time.
explanation.definitionFit: A forerunner is a predecessor, something existing before and anticipating what follows.

clue.text: Extremist Rees-Mogg elected

parts.note: Jacob Rees-Mogg is a Conservative politician, so his first name is used
a winning candidate is in office

explanation.surface: A political radical, a well-known Tory MP, has won a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacob Rees-Mogg is a famously traditionalist British Conservative MP, the opposite of a Jacobin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jacobins were radical French revolutionaries, so the word names any political extremist.

clue.text: Be outside a quiet prison

indicators.note: the first word sits outside the rest, wrapping round them

parts.note: still means quiet or silent

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay outside a peaceful jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the Paris fortress used as a state prison, stormed in 1789.

clue.text: Capri: so awfully dull

indicators.note: done awfully means done in a terrible way, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone finds the island of Capri terribly boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosaic means lacking poetry or imagination, so ordinary and uninspiring.

clue.text: Most prudish minister receiving medal

indicators.note: the minister takes in the medal, holding it within

parts.note: a priest is a minister of religion
MM is the Military Medal

explanation.surface: A very straitlaced clergyman is awarded a decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Prim means stiffly proper, so the superlative describes the most strait-laced person.

clue.text: Mark up article not consumed

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
to have eaten is to have consumed, so ate

explanation.surface: Someone marks up a piece of writing about food left uneaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To annotate a text is to add notes or comments to it, marking it up.

clue.text: Free, so vacation in province

indicators.note: letters set free are loosened from their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A holiday in a Canadian region comes at no cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Nova Scotia is one of the maritime provinces of eastern Canada.

clue.text: Check five fiery bursts

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: something that bursts explodes, scattering these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone inspects five fiery explosions.
explanation.definitionFit: To verify is to confirm or test that something is true, which is checking it.

clue.text: Athletic team's out-of-date meat

definitions.note: read as 'Athletic team is', naming the town whose club the answer is

parts.note: old means out-of-date
ham is a meat

explanation.surface: A sports team's meat is past its use-by date.
explanation.walkthrough: Oldham Athletic is an English football club from the town of Oldham, near Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: The football club is called Oldham Athletic, so the town's name identifies the Athletic team.

clue.text: One may be bent back, needing to be shortened

indicators.note: both words are cut down, leaving only a run of letters spanning them

explanation.surface: Someone's spine is bent and needs trimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like part of the definition (a bent back), but it supplies the last letter of the run.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the joint people bend, as when kneeling or proposing.

clue.text: Hung about with protective coat, I can enter

indicators.note: the letter goes into the other word, entering it

parts.note: tarred means coated with tar, a protective layer on roads and roofs

explanation.surface: Someone loitered wearing a protective layer, and gained permission to come in.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarry is to linger or delay, so tarried means lingered or dawdled.

clue.text: Young lady repelling favourite put foot in it?

parts.note: miss is a title for a young unmarried woman

indicators.note: repelling pushes back, so the word is turned backwards

parts.note: a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A young woman spurned her darling and blundered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put foot in it' is a past-tense verb; misstep works as a verb meaning to put a foot wrong, the question mark flagging the literal pun.
explanation.definitionFit: To misstep is to make a blunder, the idiom for which is putting your foot in it.

clue.text: Whisky cocktail perhaps disagreeable

definitions.meaning: a whisky ... is a cocktail, so the word stands for one example

explanation.surface: A whisky-based drink is found unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A sour is a spirit mixed with lemon and sugar; a sour mood is surly and unpleasant.

clue.text: Lungs not working? Not quite all

parts.note: a machine that is off is not working

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A medical worry about failing lungs, followed by a remark that it is not entirely total.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lungs' looks like a patient's organs failing, but it is the food sense: innards sold as meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal covers edible internal organs such as liver, heart and lungs.

clue.text: One attacking a holy book in speech

indicators.note: in speech means spoken out loud, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: a psalter is a book of psalms, with the P silent

explanation.surface: Someone assaults a scripture during an oration.
explanation.definitionFit: An assaulter is a person who physically attacks another.
